title: Drag reduction by flexibility in natural structures.
author: Bruno Alexandre Machado Almeida
abstract: In many natural structures subject to wind or water flow, drag must be limited to avoid damage: this is the case of leaves on trees and of seaweed exposed to waves. Most of the existing strategies for drag reduction in plants are based on reconfiguration, which is a significant change in shape of the object, caused by the flow itself. Typical examples are found in leaf wrapping to reduce cross flow area, or packing of seaweeds to reduce inner velocity and friction. The objective of this work to be done in LadHyX is to explore the relation between the type of deformable structure (beam, plate, and bundle) and the effectiveness of drag reduction. This will be done using experiments on deformable systems in a wind tunnel, with analysis of the flow dynamics, the change in shape and drag load. This work is part of a more general research project on plant biomechanics and fluid-structure interactions at LadHyX.
